notes:
Summary: Mid-market product company evaluating Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated migration to replace current OpenAI + homegrown caching stack. Primary goal: lower per-token cost, predictable latency for customer-facing chat and search, stronger control over models for A/B rollouts.

POC setup and scope:
- POC ran 2026-02-22 → 2026-03-09. Focus: chat (multi-turn support agent), doc-search (embeddings + reranking), streaming responses + function call parity.
- Data: 1500 support tickets, 75K docs indexed, 120 canonical prompts for parity testing.
- Baseline: running on OpenAI Enterprise with an L2 cache and basic reranker. Target p99 latency <200ms, peak concurrency 600-900 chats, throughput ~6k tokens/sec.

Findings (technical):
- Redwood Hosted (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) delivered median latency 85ms for short prompts; p95 ~180ms when batching enabled. Close to their targets but spikes during heavy batching windows.
- Prompt parity: 2/120 regression failures observed. Failures correlate with tokenization differences and Redwood safety filters tunings. Redwood SE proposed: prompt templating + explicit tokenizer normalization and Canary rollout to detect regressions.
- Reranking: initial switch to Redwood's candidate reranker caused a 3.2% drop in top-k relevance for the 'enterprise contracts' vertical. Root cause: subtle prompt formatting + model variant differences. Mitigation: fine-tune prompt templates + use reranker scoring calibration.
- Cost: Hosted run vs OpenAI baseline showed projected ~20–28% backend unit cost reduction (depends on batching & cache hit rate). Dedicated reserved pricing quoted reduces per-token further but requires 6-12 month commit.
- Compatibility layer: Redwood's OpenAI-compatible API smoothed integration for most endpoints; differences noted for function-calling semantics (edge cases) and streaming chunking that impacted existing frontend event handling.

Quotes from calls: "If two production prompts regress we can't push — need flawless parity or safe fallback" — CTO (A. Reid).
"Pricing needs to be predictable; bursts matter for us — want guaranteed tail-latency SLA" — Head of Platform.

Security & compliance:
- Requirements: SSO (SAML), SOC2, KMS (AWS KMS integration), audit logs retained 1 year (legal asks 3y for some EU customers), data residency for EU customers.
- Redwood provided SOC2 + draft addendum for data residency; still need legal sign-off on residency wording and encryption key control.

- AE discussed hybrid plan: start Hosted for broad rollout + experimentation, commit to Dedicated for peak traffic regions (NA + EU) after 3 months of stable metrics.
- Redwood provided a Dedicated pricing draft (drive link). Lunar Loom prefers a 9-month ramp with a 20% discount on committed tokens in Q1-Q3.
